newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Airbus partners mull reaction to Boeing alliance.
newsitem.headline: Airbus partners mull reaction to Boeing alliance.

text.p: The European Airbus Industrie consortium is considering how best to counter the proposed megamerger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp, one of the consortium's partners told Reuters on Friday.
"Airbus Industrie and its partner companies are still studying the implications of the deal", Anthony Parry, British Aerospace's European director, said.

Parry welcomed the speedy reaction on Wednesday from European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert who said the European Commission would have to assess whether the deal will strengthen Boeing's dominant position in Europe.
But Parry felt the surprise alliance announced on Sunday called for a review under trade policy aspects as much as under European competition rules.
"The competition policy aspects are one thing, but clearly there are also trade policy aspects that might have WTO implications," he said. He declined to elaborate.
The $13.3 billion merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas will create the world's civil and military aviation leader.
The new company will dominate the world's commercial aviation sector with 65 percent. Airbus comes far behind with 35 percent.

Industry and Commission sources and antitrust lawyers thought the assessment of Boeing's market position could not be dissociated from a review of the impact of subsidies the U.S. government gives the defence sector.

"The assessment (of the competition aspects) should be separated, but not if you say that Boeing's dominant position is reinforced by priviledged links with the Pentagon," Antoine Winckler, a partner with law firm Cleary, Gottlieb, Steen & Hamilton, told Reuters.

EU governments and the United States have accused each other of subsidising the industry. The EU side points the finger at generously calculated defence contract prices while Washington criticises Europe for directly helping Airbus and its partners.
Airbus comprises Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas.

Negotiations between the EU and the U.S. clamp down on aircraft subsidies have failed in the past. Whether the debate will be reignited will depend to a large extent on the Airbus partners and their respective governments, a Commission official said.
